text: No, the 2025 loss is not yet confirmed as persistent. While Hansen data shows a 13.5-ha tree-cover loss in 2025, corroboration requires observing the same area in a later year to confirm it hasn’t regrown. Since 2025 is the latest available year, persistence cannot be established. The loss is in a native forest context (per MGAP 2021), but its cause, legality, or responsible actor remains unknown. The JRC 2020 data confirms forest cover pre-2025, but without post-2025 observations, the loss cannot be classified as permanent.
